text:
alex: Heads-up, I'm putting forward a graceful-deprecation plan for the old controlplane bundle used by Private customers. Want to discuss rollback semantics, fallback path (peering vs endpoint relay), and per-tenant IP preservation.
maria: Nice — do you mean fully removing the monolith CP and forcing customers onto the new split-controlplane? :thinking:
alex: Yeah. The idea is phased: 1) opt-in split CP, 2) canary auto-migrate 5% of traffic, 3) enable fallback route for remaining tenants, 4) full cutover after 90d if metrics look good.
jordan: How are we handling egress IPs during canary? Many customers rely on preserved source IPs for allowlists.
alex: Plan is to preserve source IP via per-tenant SNAT mapping on the relay layer. If relay not available, fallback to legacy peering which already preserves IPs.
sam: Quick question: is fallback automatic on error or manual ops flip? We should avoid split-brain where some requests go to new CP and some to old with different auth headers.
alex: Fallback will be automatic but policy-driven. Preference order: local relay (fast), legacy peering (preserve IP), global fallback (hosted CP for public tenants). We attach request headers `x-rdw-cp-variant: v2|legacy` so we can trace.
lee: We should also add a 'graceful-degrade' header from the edge. Something like `x-rdw-degrade: allow-peering` so downstream logs can filter.
maria: Metrics to watch: error rate (5xx), p95 latency, egress-IP-change-rate (the % of sessions whose source IP changed), and auth-fail-ratio. Also watch cost delta (peering egress cost when fallback used).
jordan: For rollout, can we do tenant-level opt-in via a control API? e.g., `POST /v1/admin/tenants/:id/features` with `controlplane_variant=split`.
alex: Exactly. We'll add an admin flag and a runtime feature gate. Example command for devs to flip: ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"controlplane_variant":"split"}' \
  https://controlplane-admin.internal/v1/tenants/123/features
```
sam: If a tenant flips and then fails, what's the rollback? immediate toggle? auto-backoff?
alex: Auto-backoff policy: after 3 consecutive 5xx or latency > 2x baseline in 1 minute, we flip it back and mark the tenant for manual review. We'll emit an alert and create a ticket.
maria: Who owns the migration runbook? We need runbook steps for SRE + CSM: precheck, snapshot routing, dry-run, canary, escalate.
lee: I'll volunteer to own the runbook pages. Need a checklist: network prechecks, ACLs, KMS access, certs for relay, and egress-cost estimate.
jordan: Important: cert rotation for the relay sidecar. We should ensure the new split-controlplane accepts both cert bundles for 30 days.
alex: Good call. We'll support dual cert acceptance window and a mapper service that serves legacy TLS SNI mapping to v2 endpoints.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: controlplane-split v1.2 -> staging at 1769992500, production canary 5% at 1769993500
maria: For observability we need a quick query: find tenants with IP delta > 10% in last 24h. Can someone add a criterium to the alert rules?
lee: I'll add an alert: `egress_ip_change_ratio > 0.1` with `runbook: cp-depr-egress-ip`.
sam: One more thing — traffic shaping during the migration. We should cap burst to avoid overloading the relay pool. Suggest default per-tenant qps cap of 50 during canary.
alex: Agreed. Add runtime config: `tenant_migration_max_qps` default 50, overrideable per-tenant.
maria: Timeline idea: proposal approval this week, staging rollout + smoke 48h, canary 7d, monitor 30d, complete deprecation after 90d. Thoughts?
jordan: LGTM but add legal/compliance review for customers in regulated regions (APAC data residency). Some tenants can't move to hosted fallback.
alex: We'll exclude regulated tenants from auto-fallback and require manual migration planning.
lee: I'll draft a short migration FAQ and CSM email template.
maria: Please add a clear opt-out path and a way to pin a tenant to legacy until they finish compliance.
alex: Thanks all — I'll update the RFC doc with these action items and ping infra for relay capacity estimate. Next check-in Friday 10am.
maria: :thumbsup:
jordan: Thanks — leaving a note to SRE to prepare incident playbook.
